chapters.title: Unit 1: Measurements
chapters.description: Physical quantities, SI base units, prefixes and submultiples, parallax error prevention, and laboratory measurement tools.

concepts.title: SI Units & Physical Measurements
concepts.summary: Standard international units for length (metre), mass (kilogram), time (second), and volume (litre).
key_points: Length is measured in metres (m); 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm.
Mass is measured in kilograms (kg); beam and electronic balances measure mass accurately.
Parallax error is avoided by looking vertically above the scale reading line.

chapters.title: Unit 2: Force and Motion
chapters.description: Contact vs non-contact forces, types of motion (linear, circular, rotatory, oscillatory), and speed calculation.

concepts.title: Forces & Types of Motion
concepts.summary: Forces can push or pull, alter speed or direction; motion can be linear, circular, oscillatory, or periodic.
key_points: Contact forces require physical touch (muscular, frictional).
Non-contact forces act at a distance (gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic).
Speed = Distance / Time; measured in metres per second (m/s) or km/h.

chapters.title: Unit 3: Matter Around Us
chapters.description: Solids, liquids, gases, particle arrangement, diffusion, and separation methods for mixtures.

concepts.title: Three States of Matter & Separation of Mixtures
concepts.summary: Solids, liquids, and gases differ in particle spacing and motion; mixtures can be separated by filtration, sedimentation, and evaporation.
key_points: Solids have fixed shape and volume; particles are tightly packed.
Liquids take the shape of their container; particles slide over each other.
Gases fill all available space; particles are very far apart and move rapidly.
Insoluble solids can be separated from liquids by sedimentation, decantation, and filtration.

chapters.title: Unit 4: The World of Plants
chapters.description: Plant morphology, root systems, shoot systems, leaf anatomy, photosynthesis, transpiration, and adaptations.

concepts.title: Plant Structure & Functions
concepts.summary: Root systems absorb water and nutrients; shoot systems carry out photosynthesis, respiration, and transpiration.
key_points: Tap root system has one main thick root with lateral branches (mustard, bean).
Fibrous root system consists of a cluster of thin roots originating from stem base (grass, paddy).
Leaves produce food via photosynthesis using sunlight, chlorophyll, CO2, and water.
Transpiration releases excess water vapor through microscopic stomata.

chapters.title: Unit 5: The World of Animals
chapters.description: Unicellular vs multicellular organisms, Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena, and animal adaptations in fish, frogs, birds, and camels.

concepts.title: Animal Diversity & Adaptations
concepts.summary: Special physical and behavioral traits enabling organisms to survive in terrestrial, aquatic, or desert environments.
key_points: Amoeba moves using pseudopodia; Paramecium moves using cilia.
Fish have streamlined bodies, fins, and gills to breathe dissolved oxygen.
Birds have pneumatic hollow bones, strong flight muscles, and streamlined feathers.
Camels store fat in their humps and have broad padded feet for desert sand.

chapters.title: Unit 6: Health and Hygiene
chapters.description: Nutrients (carbs, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals), deficiency diseases, balanced diet, and communicable infections.

concepts.title: Nutrients and Deficiency Diseases
concepts.summary: Essential food components necessary for energy, body growth, and immunity against communicable pathogens.
key_points: Carbohydrates and fats are primary energy providers; proteins build body tissue.
Vitamin deficiencies: Night blindness (Vitamin A), Scurvy (Vitamin C), Rickets (Vitamin D).
Mineral deficiencies: Goitre caused by iodine deficiency; Anaemia caused by iron deficiency.

chapters.title: Unit 7: Computer — An Introduction
chapters.description: History of computers, pioneer Charles Babbage, five generations of hardware, CPU components, and input/output devices.

concepts.title: Computer Pioneers & Generations
concepts.summary: Development of electronic computation from vacuum tubes to microprocessors and modern AI systems.
key_points: Charles Babbage is known as the Father of Computing; Lady Ada Lovelace was the first computer programmer.
Hardware generations: 1st (Vacuum Tubes), 2nd (Transistors), 3rd (Integrated Circuits), 4th (Microprocessors), 5th (AI).
Central Processing Unit (CPU) contains Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU), and Memory Unit (MU).
